CONFIDENTIAL PRIVATE PLACEMENT MEMORANDUM

HARROWGATE MICROGRID PARTNERS III, LLC
Up to $60,000,000 of Class A Units
Minimum Investment: $250,000

THE SECURITIES OFFERED HEREBY HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED, OR UNDER ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS. THEY ARE OFFERED IN RELIANCE ON THE EXEMPTION PROVIDED BY SECTION 4(a)(2) OF THE ACT AND RULE 506(b) OF REGULATION D. THE SECURITIES MAY NOT BE RESOLD OR TRANSFERRED EXCEPT AS PERMITTED UNDER THE ACT AND APPLICABLE STATE LAW, PURSUANT TO REGISTRATION OR AN EXEMPTION FROM IT.

NEITHER THE SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION NOR ANY STATE SECURITIES REGULATOR HAS APPROVED OR DISAPPROVED THESE SECURITIES OR PASSED UPON THE ACCURACY OR ADEQUACY OF THIS MEMORANDUM. ANY REPRESENTATION TO THE CONTRARY IS A CRIMINAL OFFENSE.

Dated: June 1, 2026

1. SUMMARY OF THE OFFERING

The Company is offering up to 60,000 Class A Units at $1,000 per Unit, for aggregate proceeds of up to $60,000,000. The offering is made only to persons who are "accredited investors" as Rule 501(a) of Regulation D defines that term, and to no more than 35 non-accredited investors who meet the sophistication standard of Rule 506(b). The offering will terminate on the earlier of December 31, 2026 and the date the maximum offering amount is subscribed, unless the Manager extends it for up to 90 days.

2. THE COMPANY AND ITS BUSINESS

The Company was organized as a Delaware limited liability company on January 12, 2026 to acquire, develop, own, and operate behind-the-meter microgrid and battery-storage assets serving commercial and industrial hosts in the Southwest. The Company has not commenced operations, has no operating history, and has nominal assets. Its manager is Harrowgate Energy Management LLC (the "Manager").

3. USE OF PROCEEDS

Assuming the maximum offering, the Company intends to apply the proceeds approximately as follows: 78% to project acquisition and construction; 9% to a debt service reserve; 6% to the Manager's acquisition fee; 4% to organizational and offering expenses, including legal, accounting, and printing; and 3% to working capital. These allocations are estimates and the Manager may reallocate proceeds in its discretion. The Company will not use proceeds to repay indebtedness owed to the Manager or its affiliates.

4. RISK FACTORS

An investment in the Units is speculative and involves a high degree of risk, including the risk of losing the entire investment. Prospective investors should consider the following, among others.

4.1 No Operating History. The Company is newly formed, has no operating history, and has not identified all of the projects it intends to acquire. Investors must rely on the Manager's judgment.

4.2 Illiquidity. There is no public market for the Units, none is expected to develop, and the Operating Agreement restricts transfer. An investor should be prepared to hold the Units indefinitely.

4.3 Leverage. The Company expects to incur project-level debt of up to 65% of asset value. Leverage magnifies losses and a default could result in the loss of the affected project.

4.4 Conflicts of Interest. The Manager and its affiliates manage other funds with overlapping strategies, will allocate investment opportunities among them, and will receive fees from the Company whether or not investors receive distributions. The Manager's compensation was not determined at arm's length.

4.5 Regulatory. Changes to net-metering rules, interconnection standards, or the investment tax credit under Section 48E of the Internal Revenue Code could materially reduce project economics.

4.6 Tax. The Company intends to be treated as a partnership for federal income tax purposes. No ruling has been sought. Investors may recognize taxable income without a corresponding cash distribution, and will receive a Schedule K-1 that may be delivered after April 15.

4.7 Forward-Looking Statements. This Memorandum contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially, and the Company undertakes no obligation to update them.

5. TERMS OF THE OFFERING AND THE UNITS

Class A Units are entitled to a preferred return of 8% per year, cumulative and non-compounding, then a return of capital, then 80/20 distributions between Class A Units and the Manager's carried interest. Class A Units have no voting rights except on the matters the Operating Agreement specifies, including removal of the Manager for cause by holders of two-thirds of the Units.

6. COMPENSATION TO THE MANAGER AND AFFILIATES

The Manager will receive an acquisition fee of 2% of project cost, an annual asset-management fee of 1.5% of invested capital, a construction-management fee of 3% of hard costs, and the carried interest described above. The aggregate compensation is material and reduces amounts available for distribution.

7. TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS AND LEGEND

Units may not be transferred without the Manager's consent and an opinion of counsel that the transfer complies with the Act and state law. Each certificate or book-entry record will bear a restrictive legend, and investors should be aware that Rule 144 is not expected to be available.

8. SUITABILITY STANDARDS

Each investor must represent in the Subscription Agreement that it is an accredited investor, that it is acquiring the Units for its own account for investment and not with a view to distribution, that it can bear the complete loss of its investment, and that it has had the opportunity to ask questions of and receive answers from the Manager.

9. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND INVESTOR ACCESS

The Manager will make available to each prospective investor, before sale, the opportunity to ask questions and receive answers concerning the terms of the offering and to obtain any additional information the Manager possesses or can acquire without unreasonable effort or expense, as Rule 502(b) contemplates.

10. STATE LEGENDS

Residents of certain states are subject to additional restrictions. Notice filings will be made where required. This Memorandum does not constitute an offer in any jurisdiction in which an offer would be unlawful.

11. FINANCIAL INFORMATION

The Company's audited balance sheet as of March 31, 2026 is attached as Exhibit A. Because the Company is newly formed and has no operations, no statements of operations or cash flows are presented.
